title: Highly thermoelectric chitosan-based hydrogel for integrated thermal safety protection system: Cooling, overheating warning, and thermal runaway suppression in lithium-ion battery

segments.text: With the global advancement of new energy strategies, thermal safety management plays a crucial role in the development of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs).
This study synthesizes a chitosan/poly(acrylic acid-co-acrylamide)/ lignosulfonate/sodium chloride/glycerol hydrogel (CALSG) via in situ radical polymerization and solvent exchange.
This CALSG hydrogel exhibits excellent water retention and flame-retardant properties.
Additionally, it demonstrates outstanding thermoelectric property with a Seebeck coefficient of 14.52 mV/K, indicating a remarkable sensitivity to temperature variations.

Based on these integrated properties, we developed a comprehensive thermal safety protection system for LIBs that delivers three functions: cooling, overheating warning, and thermal runaway (TR) suppression.

This system not only maintains LIBs within a safe operating temperature range but also triggers an alarm once the battery surface temperature surpasses a predefined threshold, thereby mitigating potential safety hazards.
In the event of TR, this CALSG hydrogel effectively suppresses TR propagation and partially blocks the spreading sparks and jet flames, providing time for emergency response.
This approach presents a promising solution to address thermal safety concerns in LIBs, underscoring the potential of ionic hydrogels in enhancing the safety and reliability of LIB applications.

title: First-principle investigation of physical properties of Li2MgMH6 (M = Zn & Cd) double perovskite hydrides for solid-state hydrogen storage and some other applications

segments.text: First-principle calculations of structural, hydrogen storage, mechanical, electronic, optical, and thermoelectric properties of Li2MgZnH6 and Li2MgCdH6 perovskite hydrides are reported.
Both specimens are stable in a cubic structure.
They also show thermodynamic, dynamical, and mechanical stability.
They would be efficient solidstate hydrogen storage materials due to high gravimetric and volumetric hydrogen densities and suitable desorption temperatures.
Both perovskite hydrides are elastically anisotropic and ductile, show dominance of ionic bonding over the covalent, and possess fairly high melting temperatures and inferior thermal conductivity.

Both Li2MgZnH6 and Li2MgCdH6 are wide and direct (Gamma-Gamma) band gap semiconductors of band gaps 3.13 and 2.73 eV, which correspond to the violet and blue-green region of the visible spectrum, respectively.
Electrons possess a lower effective mass and hence better mobility compared to holes in these specimens.
Calculated optical properties of these semiconductors show high optical absorption in the Extreme Ultraviolet (EUV) region.

The optical energy gap of each specimen is slightly higher than the corresponding minimum band gap and they lie in the topmost part of the UV region and violet region of the visible spectrum, respectively.

Therefore, calculated optoelectronic properties and significant optical absorption in the UV region reveal that Li2MgZnH6 and Li2MgCdH6 could serve as promising semiconductors in manufacturing different UV optoelectronic devices.

Calculated thermoelectric properties show that both p-type Li2MgZnH6 and Li2MgCdH6 could be much more effective thermoelectric materials at the mid-temperature region 500-600 K for renewable energy technologies due to a higher value of ZT of p-type compared to n-type Li2MgZnH6 and Li2MgCdH6, though their thermoelectric efficiencies are insufficient for many practical applications.

title: Elucidating the Structural, Electronic, Magnetic, Mechanical, Thermoelectric, and Thermodynamic Properties of TbCo4 X 12 (X = P, Sb) for Advanced Applications

segments.text: In this piece of investigation, TbCo4 X (12) (X = P, Sb) Terbium -filled, Skutterudites have been precisely reported through DFT ab-initio calculations in the Trans Bhala modified Becke-Johnson (TB-mBJ) potential to extract the electronic, mechanical, along with thermal, and transport properties.
Structural stability was confirmed through ground state energy calculations using the Birch-Murnaghan equation of state.

Electronic structure analysis, combining Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof Generalized Gradient Approximation (PBE-GGA) and Trans Bhala modified Becke Johnson (TB-mBJ) functionals, revealed a metallic nature with PBE-GGA and a half-metallic character with TB-mBJ.
Specifically, energy gaps of 0.24 eV and 0.64 eV were determined for TbCo4 X (12 )and TbCo4 X (12), respectively.
Mechanical property calculations indicated a brittle nature for both compounds.
Charge density analysis confirmed ionic bonding characteristics, suggesting chemical stability.
High Seebeck coefficient (S) values and associated figure of merit (zT) suggest promising thermoelectric performance across a broad temperature range.

context_quotes: Electronic structure analysis, combining Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof Generalized Gradient Approximation (PBE-GGA) and Trans Bhala modified Becke Johnson (TB-mBJ) functionals, revealed a metallic nature with PBE-GGA and a half-metallic character with TB-mBJ.
modality_evidence: In this piece of investigation, TbCo4 X (12) (X = P, Sb) Terbium -filled, Skutterudites have been precisely reported through DFT ab-initio calculations in the Trans Bhala modified Becke-Johnson (TB-mBJ) potential to extract the electronic, mechanical, along with thermal, and transport properties.

Electronic structure analysis, combining Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof Generalized Gradient Approximation (PBE-GGA) and Trans Bhala modified Becke Johnson (TB-mBJ) functionals, revealed a metallic nature with PBE-GGA and a half-metallic character with TB-mBJ.
